title: Introduce invocation timeline slab aggregation and log fidelity controller
author: Samir Patel
description:
Context & motivation: We have good end-to-end latency and token-cost metrics, but it is still hard to attribute where time and tokens are spent inside long/complex invocations (prompt preprocessing, KV cache lookup, model kernel warmup, decoding burst). This PR introduces a lightweight "slab" aggregation for invocation timelines plus a dynamic Log Fidelity Controller that adjusts logging/sampling fidelity based on observed slab variance. Goals: 1) produce per-invocation timeline slabs that attribute latency and token counts to logical phases, 2) expose slab rollups and percentiles to the Console, 3) reduce noise and log volume while increasing signal for anomalous invocations via a runtime fidelity controller, and 4) provide an alert tuning recipe (slope-based) that ties SLOs to slab-derived percentiles.

What this change does (high level):
- Adds a slab aggregator in the serving runtime that slices an invocation into chronological slabs (parse, cache-lookup, fetch, decode) with per-slab token and latency counters. Slabs are bounded by a small finite state machine and low-memory per-invocation footprint.
- Emits compact slab spans (summary spans) alongside regular traces so we can correlate trace edges to slab boundaries without storing full per-token spans.
- Introduces a Log Fidelity Controller service that subscribes to slab rollups; it maintains a per-route fidelity score and issues sampling directives to the logging pipeline (higher fidelity for routes or tenants exhibiting high slab variance or rising decode latencies).
- Adds dashboard artifacts (Console panels) for slab percentile rollups, slab-cohort trend lines, and a slope-based alert recipe that detects rapid increases in decode-slab p95 over a 10-minute window.
- Includes unit and integration tests for slab aggregation, and a small simulation harness used in perf bench runs.

Design notes and tradeoffs: the slab boundary FSM is conservative — it prioritizes stability and low overhead over perfect semantic segmentation; we intentionally avoid emitting per-token spans (too heavy). The fidelity controller is policy driven and can be disabled per-tenant via config.

Rollout plan:
- Stage 1 (canary): enable slab emission for 5% of traffic in us-west-2; fidelity controller runs in passive mode (suggestions only).
- Stage 2 (ramp): enable 25% with active fidelity directives for selected routes, monitor logging volume delta and slab-percentile SLOs.
- Stage 3: global when telemetry shows under 7% log-volume growth and improved signal-to-noise in alerts.

Operational playbook (short):
- New Console panels: Invocation Timeline Slabs (per-route) and Slab Variance Heatmap. Use the "slab-decomp" explorer to drill into anomalous windows.
- Alerts: the introduced rule "DecodeSlab:P95:Slope" triggers when p95 slope > 1.5x baseline over 10m; it includes an auto-mute for known maintenance windows.

Related work: complements ENG-4190 (kv-cache profiler) and ENG-4155 (token-cost rollups). Linked Linear: ENG-4219 (slab aggregation), ENG-4230 (log fidelity controller).

Checklist:
- [x] Runtime slab aggregator and summary spans
- [x] Fidelity controller and policy config
- [x] Console dashboard JSON and panels
- [x] Unit + integration tests
- [x] Perf bench harness + initial numbers (attached below)

Perf numbers (canary sample): slab aggregator adds ~1.2% p50 CPU and 0.6% p50 memory on host; end-to-end p95 token latency attribution error < 3% vs trace-level ground truth in our sim harness.

- Console dashboard (preview): https://console.internal.redwood/dashboards/slab-invocation-preview
- Linear: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4219

commits: Initial slab aggregator and FSM implementation (serving/runtime/telemetry)
Add summary span emission and trace correlation hooks
Log Fidelity Controller: policy engine, controller loop, and SDK integration
Console: add slab dashboard JSON and panel configs

Fix: reduce memory allocation in slab buffer and add defensive nil checks
review_comments: Hannah Li: This looks promising — what's the worst-case memory blowup per invocation? We need hard limits to avoid OOMs on high-concurrency hosts.
Samir Patel (author): Answered: slab buffer is preallocated to 4 entries by default and uses a small ring buffer; added defensive caps and a guard metric 'slab_buffer_dropped' to track drops.
Diego Ramos: Can we get an example of a slab decomposition for a long-running chain? I want to ensure we don't attribute model-side stalls incorrectly.
Samir Patel: Added docs section with example decomposition for a 3-step chain and notes on how we detect stalls (time thresholds and kernel-wait flags).
Priya Nair: The slope-based alert looks sensitive; can we add a cooldown and a tenant-scoped exemption list?
Samir Patel: Added cooldown (5m) and tenant exemption config; also added an alert mute annotation in the generated alert payload.
release_notes: Observability: Add invocation timeline slab aggregation to attribute latency and tokens to logical invocation phases.
Observability: Add Log Fidelity Controller to dynamically adjust logging sampling based on slab variance.
Console: New dashboard panels for slab percentile rollups and variance heatmap.
Alerts: New slope-based decode-slab p95 alert with cooldown and tenant exemptions.
merge_summary: Merged by Hannah Li (squash merge). Squashed commit message: 'obs: add invocation timeline slab aggregation + log fidelity controller — ENG-4219, ENG-4230' — No conflicts. Canary rollout plan added to release notes.
notes_for_ops: If false positives spike after rollout, disable the fidelity controller (telemetry.fidelity.enabled=false) and revert to sampled slab rollups. Watch 'slab_buffer_dropped' metric and alert at >1% drop rate across hosts.
